deep.reconstruction:
Page 1 of a manuscript headed 'Hyperrecouvrements' (archive p.10). Setting: X is a U-topos and A a small category. Grothendieck proposes to call a 'hypercovering of X indexed by A' a functor phi: A -> X, alpha |-> U_alpha, subject to conditions inspired by the Čech-style yoga of coverings and by its refinement suggested by Cartier for non-paracompact spaces. That refinement is the hypercovering technique, which Verdier credits to Cartier in SGA4 V.7.

Hyp 1: the family (U_alpha -> e_X), for alpha in Ob A, is epimorphic (covering) onto the final object.

Hyp 1' (struck out): for each alpha_0, the induced functor A/alpha_0 -> X/U_{alpha_0} satisfies Hyp 1. That is, the maps U_alpha -> U_{alpha_0} indexed by arrows alpha -> alpha_0 form a covering family. The sentence ends 'reste couvrant' on the next page.

Next page, Hyp 2: for alpha, beta in A, the arrows U_gamma -> U_alpha x U_beta, indexed by spans alpha <- gamma -> beta (objects of A/(alpha x beta), product taken in A^), form a covering family. The generalized version does the same for finite families alpha_0, ..., alpha_n. Grothendieck observes:
- n=0 recovers Hyp 1';
- the generalized Hyp 2 follows from Hyp 1' + Hyp 2 by induction, because a composite of covering families is covering, and covering families are stable under product with an identity.

In modern terms, Hyp 1 + Hyp 2 are exactly the first two of the three 'internal filteredness' conditions for a functor A -> E. These are SGA4 IV 4.9 / Mac Lane–Moerdijk VII.8 'filtering' or 'flat' functors. The missing third condition, presumably still to come, concerns parallel arrows u, v: alpha => beta and requires the U_gamma for gamma -> alpha equalizing u, v to cover Eq(U(u), U(v)). With it, phi corresponds to a geometric morphism X -> Â (presheaves on A). So the notion being set up is 'a covering of the topos shaped like A' = a geometric morphism from X to the presheaf topos of A. Because U_alpha need not be representable or simplicial, this generalizes Čech covers (A = discrete or ordered simplices) and simplicial hypercovers (A = Δ-type categories). In a manuscript on stratified topoi, the natural specialization is A = a poset of strata. There a geometric morphism X -> P^ (Alexandrov topos) is precisely the modern notion of a P-stratification of X.
errors: Hyp 1' (and hence the n=0 case of the generalized Hyp 2 on the next page) is automatically satisfied: A/alpha_0 contains the identity of alpha_0, so the family includes id: U_{alpha_0} -> U_{alpha_0}, which is trivially covering. This is likely why Hyp 1' was crossed out. The genuinely nontrivial 'n=-1' case is Hyp 1 (empty product = final object). As a result, the next page's claim 'Hyp 1' + Hyp 2 ⇒ generalized Hyp 2' really reduces to 'Hyp 2 ⇒ generalized Hyp 2 for n ≥ 1', which the induction shows correctly.

The listed conditions (Hyp 1, Hyp 2) do not yet include the equalizer condition for parallel arrows. Without it, the definition is weaker than flatness or filteredness when A has non-trivial parallel arrows. For posets, or when A has no parallel pairs, it is harmless.

ideas.what: Hypercovering of a topos indexed by an arbitrary small category A, defined as a functor A -> X with covering conditions
ideas.modern_name: Flat / internally filtered functor A -> X, equivalently a geometric morphism X -> PSh(A); generalized hypercover
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hypercoverings: Cartier/Verdier (SGA4 V, 1963-64); flat functors and geometric morphisms into presheaf topoi: SGA4 IV (Grothendieck–Verdier), Diaconescu (1975)
ideas.where_published: SGA4 Exp. IV 4.9 (flat functors / points), Exp. V.7 (hypercoverings, Verdier)

ideas.what: Covering conditions: the U_alpha cover 1; for each pair alpha, beta the U_gamma over spans cover U_alpha x U_beta; finite generalization by induction using composition of covering families
ideas.modern_name: Filteredness conditions (i),(ii) for flat functors into a topos
ideas.usually_credited_to: SGA4 IV; Mac Lane–Moerdijk ch. VII

ideas.what: Attribution of the refinement of Čech methods for non-paracompact spaces to Cartier
ideas.where_published: SGA4 V (Verdier); mentioned in Récoltes et Semailles context

missed.claim: In a manuscript titled 'Topos stratifié', Grothendieck frames 'hypercoverings' as functors from an arbitrary small category A into the topos satisfying flatness-type covering conditions, i.e. geometric morphisms X -> Â. Specialized to A a poset, this is exactly the now-standard definition of a P-stratified topos/∞-topos as a geometric morphism to the Alexandrov topos of P (Lurie HA A.5; Barwick–Glasman–Haine, Exodromy). The page suggests Grothendieck was approaching stratifications and Čech/hypercover descent through one common 'A-indexed covering' notion. Whether he made that identification explicitly cannot be read off this page.
missed.quote: On peut définir la notion d'hyperrecouvrement de X ... indexé par une petite catégorie A. Ce sera par définition un foncteur φ : A → X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it would show an early (1981+) unification of covering-indexed descent with stratification-as-geometric-morphism-to-a-poset-topos, predating the exodromy literature. Mathematically it is standard, so the interest is mainly historiographic.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is a restatement of the flat/filtering functor conditions from SGA4 and the Cartier–Verdier hypercover idea; the only mild interest is the context, namely category-indexed covers in a stratified-topos manuscript, which hints at the later geometric-morphism-to-poset-topos view of stratifications.
transcription_corrections: 'y.g.' should read 'yoga' ('le raffinement de ce yoga suggéré par Cartier').
The inserted word above 'des' is plausibly 'Čechiste' (or 'cechiste'); this is consistent with the image.

The left-margin note is hard to read; it seems to be a question whether the struck-out condition follows from the others (something like 'Est-ce que ça se déduit de ... ? i.e.!'). The machine reading 'sous Hyp 1 ça découle' is uncertain.
The archive page number '10' in the left margin is a cataloguing mark, not part of the text; the manuscript's own page number is '1'.
